title: The Concept of Cognitive Dissonance
text:
Cognitive dissonance describes the mental discomfort experienced by a person who holds two or more conflicting beliefs, ideas, or values, or when their actions conflict with their existing beliefs. Because this inconsistency generates psychological tension, individuals are strongly motivated to reduce the dissonance and achieve internal consistency.

Reduction of this uncomfortable state can occur in several ways: through changing one's behavior (the most difficult route), altering one of the conflicting beliefs, or, most commonly, adding new cognitions that rationalize or justify the disparity. For instance, a smoker who believes smoking is harmful might reduce dissonance by focusing on limited scientific studies suggesting alternative risks.
